description: Sync daily search performance for one Google Search Console property, one document per report row with clicks, impressions, click-through rate and average position.
opening: Sync daily search performance reports for one Search Console property. Each report row is one small document: one day for one search query, page, country or device, or one day for the whole property, with its clicks, impressions, click-through rate and average position. A busy site produces one document per query per day.

Search Console permissions are not imported, so every synced row is visible to everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. Only web search performance is read. Rows that drop out of a later report stay in HydraDB.

connect.auth: Search Console uses a Google service-account JSON key together with the property to read.

credentials.name: client_secrets
credentials.text: The service account's JSON key, pasted whole.

credentials.name: site_url
credentials.text: The Search Console property to read, written as Search Console names it: a URL-prefix property such as `https://example.com/`, or a domain property such as `sc-domain:example.com`.

steps.title: Create a service account key
steps.text: In Google Cloud, create a service account and download its JSON key.

steps.title: Create the connector
steps.text: Paste the key as `client_secrets` and the property as `site_url`.

steps.title: Select the property
steps.text: HydraDB lists one `All data` resource for the property. Select it. Report types cannot be selected separately.

connect.account: One connector reads one Search Console property.

sync.first_sync: Reaches back the window set by `lookback_days`, 30 days by default.
sync.changes: Each sync reads the days since the last sync, plus the three days before them again. The current UTC day is not read until the next day. The freshest data Search Console has, which can still change, is included.
sync.edits: Rows for the three re-read days replace their earlier documents, so late changes Search Console makes to those days come across.
sync.deletes: Rows are never removed. A row that drops out of a later report stays searchable in HydraDB.
notes: On a day with more than 50,000 rows in one report, some of that day's rows are skipped.

documents.name: Report rows
documents.one_document: One day of one report: one search query, one page, one country or one device, or the whole property for that day.
documents.title: For a query row, the query in quotes followed by ` - search performance (<date>)`. For a page, country, device or keys row, the value followed by ` - search performance (<date>)`. For a whole-property row, `Search performance for <site> (<date>)`.
documents.text: The title, then `Site`, the row's own line (`Query`, `Page`, `Country`, `Device` or `Keys`), `Date`, `Clicks`, `Impressions`, `CTR` and `Avg position` lines. `CTR` is a percentage with two decimals and `Avg position` has one decimal. Empty values are left out.
documents.date: The report day, at midnight UTC.

attributes.name: query, page, country, device, keys
attributes.text: The value the row reports on, written into the title and its own line. The keys report asks only for the date, so its rows repeat the whole-property daily totals.

attributes.name: clicks, impressions, ctr, position
attributes.text: The day's metrics, written as the `Clicks`, `Impressions`, `CTR` and `Avg position` lines.

attributes.name: date
attributes.text: The report day. It is written into the title and the `Date` line and sets the result date.

attributes.name: site_url
attributes.text: The property, written into the `Site` line with everything up to the first colon removed. `https://example.com/` reads as `//example.com/` and `sc-domain:example.com` reads as `example.com`.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.google_search_console_stream
attributes.text: The report the row came from: `performance_report_query`, `performance_report_page`, `performance_report_date`, `performance_report_country`, `performance_report_device` or `performance_report_keys`. Limits a query to one report, for example only per-query rows. Not searchable.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's rows. Not searchable.

attributes.name: provider
attributes.text: Always `google-search-console`, with hyphens. A filter on `google_search_console` matches nothing. Not searchable.

attributes.name: stream_type
attributes.text: The report the row came from, shown when you inspect the item. To limit a query to one report, use `additional_metadata.google_search_console_stream`.

example_searches: How did the search query "running shoes" perform on 2026-11-03?
How many clicks and impressions did the /pricing page get on 2026-11-03?
What was our average position on mobile devices last week?

connections: None. Rows are not linked to each other, to pages or to the property.
graph.people: No people or groups are attached to rows.
graph.from_text: The report text: the site, the query, page, country or device, the date and the metrics.

not_synced: Image, video and news search performance. Only web search is read.
URL inspection, index coverage, sitemaps and other Search Console reports.
Query and page pairs as one combined report.
Properties other than the one set in `site_url`.
Removals: rows that drop out of a later report stay in HydraDB.
